status: Estimated and benchmarked context for the Scenario Lab; the deterministic case model is unchanged and every figure here recomputes from the archived sources below.

originSweep.verdict: The fitted trend ranges from 6.7% to 16.6% per month depending only on the start month; no single fitted growth rate is the trend.

elasticity.reading: Statistically zero at both frequencies; compression is an assumption the data cannot reject, not a measured elasticity.

capture.caveat: Capture was rising before the fee switch, so the pre/post split measures a continuing trend, not a clean step; attribution to the switch is confounded and the test assumes iid on a trending series.

econ.note: Eleven complete months and ten growth observations; every statistic is noisy and the bootstrap intervals are honest about it.

calibration.process: log V_{m+1} = log V_m + mu_case + sigma*z + J
calibration.defaultSpec: Single Gaussian with sigma=rawAllMonths; the explicit-jump variant is an upside stress only and must pair with sigma=exJumpMonths, never with rawAllMonths.

conclusions: Realized volume escaped the Bear-Maximum envelope upward in 7 of 8 holdout months at the May and July cutoffs; every case under-projected cumulative volume by 23-42%. The September cutoff then whipsawed: October fell below even Bear.
Error concentrates in jump months: case MAPE 1-15% in the calm month versus 28-40% pooled across jump months.
A log-linear trend fitted at each cutoff beat no fixed case out of sample; it extrapolated flat exactly when the regime flipped.
A lognormal 10-90% band around Base covered 6 of 9 holdout months against an 80% nominal target (small sample, indicative only).

rollingOrigin.source: DefiLlama dexs/near-intents daily volume, first day 2024-12-10
rollingOrigin.design: Every complete month end is a forecast origin. The trailing 30-day average daily volume at the origin is projected forward under each fixed case growth rate and compared with realized average daily volume 1 to 6 months later. The 80% band uses only growth volatility observed up to the origin.

regimes.launchYear: Origins through 2025-11, the first twelve months after launch

duneCrossCheck.note: DefiLlama monthly volume divided by the Dune series used elsewhere in the lab, over the months both cover.

rollingOrigin.bootstrap: Medians recomputed on 5,000 resamples of whole origins, because forecasts from one origin share a baseline and overlapping horizons; seeded with the lab seed plus 7.
conclusions: After the launch year the Base path showed no detectable bias: across 45 forecasts from 10 origins, realized volume landed a median +0.1% from Base. Forecasts from one origin overlap, so the honest sample is 10 origins, and resampling whole origins gives a 90% interval of −17.2% to +21.9%.
The fixed cases were too narrow: only 12 of 45 outcomes fell between Bear and Maximum, with 18 above Maximum and 15 below Bear. Month-to-month swings are wider than the whole case range.

The uncertainty band the lab draws (σ = 0.2362 a month) covered 40 of 45 second-year outcomes against an 80% target. Its σ is measured over these same months, so this is an in-sample check. A band using only volatility known at each origin covered 45 of 45, because launch-year swings inflate it.
In the launch year volume beat Maximum in 57 of 66 forecasts. That ramp from near zero is a different regime and is not evidence for or against the 2031 cases.
DefiLlama, which supplies the full history, matches the Dune series used elsewhere in the lab to a median ratio of 0.999 over 11 shared months (range 0.87–1.02).

excluded.name: Morpho
excluded.reason: missing market cap or zero revenue

nearSpecific.note: The model multiple applies to captured Intents receipts; DefiLlama chain revenue counts burned gas only, a roughly twenty-fold smaller denominator.

anchor.finding: Xu, Xu and Lommers value DeFi tokens on holders-revenue multiples, find DeFi converging toward roughly tenfold TradFi levels by mid-2022 and conclude DeFi tokens were overpriced relative to financial-services equity.

caveats: Ethena revenue covers only its recent fee-switch window, so its multiple is not comparable.
Jito holders revenue and Sui thirty-day revenue are near zero; those multiples are denominators artifacts.
Chain revenue on DefiLlama is the burned or validator-captured slice and is not comparable with protocol fee capture.

requiredReturnTable.label: Realized BTC, post-ETF window
requiredReturnTable.basis: Geometric annualized BTC return minus the window-average five-year Treasury yield, computed from the archived series.

requiredReturnTable.label: Realized BTC since 2020
requiredReturnTable.basis: Long-window realized return; inflated by early-cycle growth and backward-looking.

requiredReturnTable.label: Brigida latent-factor estimate
requiredReturnTable.basis: arXiv:2601.07664, three-pass latent-factor price of crypto market risk, annualized 24.5% (p = 0.062).

requiredReturnTable.label: Brigida Fama-MacBeth estimate
requiredReturnTable.basis: arXiv:2601.07664, 0.116% per week annualized (p < 0.001); the paper shows this naive estimate is biased by omitted factors.

requiredReturnTable.label: Borri et al. 2022 estimate
requiredReturnTable.basis: As quoted in arXiv:2601.07664: a similar annualized crypto market premium of 26%.

rate.reading: Formal cross-sectional premium estimates give a required return near 36-41%; the selected 26.3% hurdle sits at the bottom of that defensible range and inside the 25-35% bridge-stage venture band.
caveats: BTC understates total-crypto-market beta; the BTC+ETH blend only partly mitigates this.
Short-window realized premia are noise-dominated; long-window realized premia are inflated by early-cycle hypergrowth. The spread across variants is the finding.
Weekly returns are sampled in seven-day blocks back from the last complete candle.
